items.name: The Vault
items.notes: Vanguard+Swap body-then-become run. Signature: the king lives in a sealed stone strongbox; knight-jump squares are walled so a dropped body can only create a landing. Finale L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, vanguard+swap 81-97%. Full runs 28% random / 53% with the pair.

items.name: The Switchback
items.notes: Poison Dart + Bishop Squire free-capture-stun run. Signature: two stone bars on ranks 3 and 6 with offset openings, so every level charges moves to arrive. Finale: a sealed diagonal room reached only through a corridor guarded by an uncapturable pawn — dart it, and summon the Squire into the corridor the turn it dies. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 63-100%. Full runs 18% random / 33% with the pair (below target; L8 is the drag).

items.name: The Briar
items.notes: Dragon + Sacrifice parachute-the-bomb run. Signature: a two-deep pawn hedge on ranks 6-7 where the back row defends the front and a rook capture is always recaptured. A dragon spawned beside the hedge and detonated the same turn opens the two files beside Rookie top to bottom and stuns the king. L7-L10: every single kit card 0-3%, pair 78-84%. Full runs 55% random / 50% with the pair (random converges on the pair since it is half the kit).

items.name: The Glasshouse
items.notes: Freeze Ray + Vanguard pin-and-parachute run. Signature: a box of hazards around the king's corner with one missing pane that something is watching; from L7 he bricks the window up and the only sightline left is his. Finale: freeze him where he stands, drop the knight, walk it on, take him inside the pin. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 72-100% (serial reads). Full runs 43% random / 70% with the pair.

items.name: The Stacks
items.notes: Magnet + Boulder reposition-then-seal run. Signature: ranks 3-7 are solid stone with one-wide shafts, so one piece closes a whole route and every level asks which square an enemy stands on. A bishop in a shaft is frozen (a plug only a pull can move); the king's 2x2 corner room can never be held by a lone rook. Finale: boulder a stone into the room, magnet the plug off its defenders, take it free. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 97-100% (serial). Full runs 35% random / 25% with the pair — the pair pool is LOWER than random because upgraded high-tier Boulder walls Rookie's own shaft.

items.name: The Cliff
items.notes: Convert + Summon Knight cage-and-take run, a pair the discovery harness found. Signature: one diagonal of stone a rook can never cross and a knight steps over. Finale: convert the pawn under the king's pen so his own guard becomes the cage, then the Squire jumps in and takes him. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 75-88% (serial). Full runs 8% random / 13% with the pair (L3 is a Squire-or-nothing gate). 2026-09-06 CONVERT REWORK: converted pieces are now controllable summons, and the stolen guard pawn (a7 / g7) attacks the king's square, so Convert ALONE now clears L7 and L8 at 100% (even with the same-turn daze — it strikes a turn later and he cannot step off) (L9/L10 still 0% single, pair 84-88%). Finale no longer combo-gated on L7-L8 — demoted testing → built until L7/L8 are redesigned (the guard under the pen must not attack the pen).

items.name: The Slash
items.notes: Boulder + Knight Hop cage-and-take run. Signature: one diagonal of stone corner to corner that only a knight crosses. Finale: jump the slash, drop two stones on the king's flight squares, slide onto his line. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 100% (serial). Full runs 40% random / 85% with the pair. Boulder earned its place: the stone's job is one turn deep, which the bot models.

items.name: The Millstone
items.notes: Dragon + Duchess double-door run. Signature: the king lives on a four-square diamond around a stone pillar; the finale is a double door where one body opens it once and dies, and the second body walks through. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 72-88% (serial). Full runs 18% random / 45% with the pair. Tier caveat: at 2 charges one summon can trade twice alone.

items.name: The Parapet
items.notes: Knight Hop + Twin run. Signature: rank 6 is solid stone every level; the court is ranks 7-8. Finale: hop onto a square no rook line reaches, summon the Twin beside her, two rooks close the 2x2. L7-L10: every single kit card 0%, pair 100% (serial). Full runs 33% random / 65% with the pair. TIER CAVEAT: knight-hop at T4 (two uses) solos L7-L9 at 78-97%; the gate holds at T1-T3 and T5.

items.name: The Alley
items.notes: Smoke + Rabies Dart (blind the court). HONEST MISS: the finale does not meet the combo gate at T1 cards (rabies alone 53% on L7; pair 63/9/6/9). The pair is a T5 story the harness cannot measure and the bot cannot plan cast-then-wait lines. Kept as idea; reachable via ?run=revenge-20, not on the playtest page.

items.name: The Lattice
items.notes: Duchess + Decoy (buy the body time) — the first designed home for either card. Signature: ranks 5-8 are stone on the DARK squares only, a checkerboard of panes, so no rook line survives up there (a king on a light square of ranks 6-8 can never be captured by Rookie) while the light diagonals run straight through and his pawns are frozen but still bite. L1-L2 ride an open channel; L3-L5 a defended cork (aegis/decoy 100%, magnet is the trap at 6-31%); L6 the panes close and the Duchess alone is the only thing that can reach him (100%, everything else 0%). L7-L10 add a WATCHER pawn on the one square that attacks him: the Duchess lands there and is eaten, so mark a pawn defended by a jammed bishop (threat 2 beats the watcher's 1, deterministically) and the court spends its whole turn eating its own man. Finale numbers of record (Normal, T5, --jobs=1 --trials=32): none 0%, aegis 0%, magnet 0%, decoy 0%, duchess 0% on all four levels; duchess+decoy 100/97/100/100. Every other kit pair 0% on all four — four unique-answer levels. Full runs 13/40 = 33% with random picks (all deaths move-limit at L6-L7), 35/40 = 88% with the pair as the pool. TIER CAVEAT: the gate holds at T1-T3 and breaks at T4+, where the Duchess gets a second charge and the body that re-takes the plugged post is unanswerable — the post can never have a spare defender because the only squares attacking it are the king's own and the watcher's.

items.name: The Alcove
items.notes: Become King + Boulder (untouchable engineer) — the first run built on that pair. SIGNATURE: the king stands in a one-square-wide stone alcove on an edge file where every orthogonal line in and out is sealed; a stump SENTRY pawn covers the DOORSTEP beneath him (the only square that attacks him), one diagonal-up CORNER is bricked at build time and the other is his single flight square, unreachable forever. From L6 a SILL closes the doorstep's file, so no rook line in the game reaches it and the only way on is a diagonal step from a launch square. FINALE LINE: reach a launch square, then in one turn cast Become King (free), drop a stone on the corner (free), and step onto the doorstep — he cannot run, the sentry bounces off her royal hide, she reverts to a rook on the doorstep and slides onto him. SERIAL NUMBERS OF RECORD (Normal, T5 bot, kit at T1, jobs=1, 32 trials, L7-L10): no-ability 0/0/0/0, become-king alone 0/0/0/0, boulder alone 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, the PAIR 91/97/81/81. Mid-run single-card keys all clear at 100% with the right card (L3+L4 aegis, L5 boulder, L6 become-king). FULL RUNS: 14/40 = 35% with random picks from the kit (all deaths move-limit, arriving without the level's card), 16/40 = 40% with the pair-only pool — 13 of those 20 losses are on L4, whose key is aegis and which the pair-only pool cannot hold. TIER CAVEAT: the gate is exact at T1 and gone at T3 — become-king:4 alone reads 100% on all four finale levels, because two king moves let her take the corner diagonally from his vacated square; boulder:4 / aegis:4 / magnet:4 all still read 0%. Same family as the Colonnade's T4 Bishop Squire; pinning Become King's tier in this run would restore it.

items.name: The Keep
items.notes: Signature pair BECOME KING + BOULDER (untouchable engineer) — NOTE: this pair collided with THE ALCOVE (revenge-25), which shipped from another session while this run was being measured, so this one is registered as an IDEA and deliberately NOT pushed to the playtest page; Tyler's call whether a second run on the same pair is wanted. Constant signature: the king's room is a RING of squares around a stone PILLAR, sealed by a stone lip with one gap, and from L5 on that gap is DIAGONAL — its whole rank and file are stone, so no rook move in the game can end on it and only a king steps in — with his last pawn, walled on its own rank and file so nothing can ever capture it, covering the doorway. Finale line: stone the two ring squares behind him (the two the king-arc cannot reach), cast Become King, step diagonally into the doorway, let the pawn's reply bounce off, and take him with the rook the crown turns back into. Serial numbers of record (Normal, jobs=1, 32 trials, L7-L10): 0% for no-ability AND 0% for every single kit card (become-king, boulder, aegis, magnet), pair 84/84/91/78%. No tier caveat — at become-king:5 / boulder:5 / aegis:5 / magnet:5 every single card still reads 0% on all four levels, the first Revenge finale that is not tier-fragile, because the gate is a square a rook cannot reach rather than a count of stones or turns. Full runs: 10/40 = 25% random picks (first combo run inside the Moat's 10-25% band; attrition is mid-run at L3/L4/L5) and 20/40 = 50% with the pair pool. Mid-run keys: L3/L6 Boulder, L4 Aegis, L5 Become King, Magnet the pure trap. MISSES the two rubric lines Tyler added 2026-09-06: the pair reads above the new 60-80% band on three of four levels, and L7-L10 are one line four times.

items.name: Snare
items.notes: Set a trap on an empty square (free action). Invisible to the enemy AI. The first enemy to arrive on it during the enemy phase (a flee step, an approach, a Magnet pull, a Coup swap) is held there: frozen for the tier's hold (1/2/2/3/3 turns). From T4 a guard that springs it is captured instead (credited to Rookie, king stunned 2 turns); the king is only ever held. Consumed on springing; T5 re-arms. The boulder trick with the sign flipped: let him take his flight square and keep him there. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: Shove
items.notes: Push a stone beside Rookie one square directly away from her (free action). It moves; it does not disappear: a gap opens where it was, a square dies where it lands (a pen square becomes a hazard he cannot step to). Legal only when the landing square is empty; from T3 a pawn it lands on is crushed (a Rookie capture with the king stun); T4 reaches stones two squares off on her rook lines; T5 unlimited. Never a shove that leaves Rookie with no move; never into a stone (two-thick walls are shove-proof); authored stones marked fixed cannot be pushed. Universal-solvent class: keep out of terrain kits unless it is half the signature pair. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: Coup
items.notes: Trade the king's square with one of his own guards (free action): his man takes the throne, he takes the post. T1 a pawn beside him; T2 any guard beside him; T3-T4 any guard in his room or within 2; T5 any enemy on the board. T4+ the swap stuns him a turn. Poison, rabies, frozen and decoy markers ride with their pieces; his pen gains the post square so he is never outside the rules, but his throne is now plugged by his own guard. Guards stand on posts because posts have lines to them; the second beat is a line he cannot step off, a stone on his step back, a snare, or a body's cover. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: Hourglass
items.notes: REWORKED + GRADED 2026-09-06. Turn the glass (free action): the enemies take a full turn now and Rookie's move is still in hand. ONE RULE - a glass-turn is a turn taken out of ROOKIE'S clock: moveCount does not tick and nothing of hers expires during it (freeze/snare holds, the king's stun, smoke, the straw, decoy, rabies, king-form, summon clocks, a convert daze, the once-per-turn summon move). Only POISON still burns - a fuse is a bomb going off, not a protection running out. The king REACTS on a glass-turn at every tier (the old T3 hold-the-king clause is deleted: an upgrade must never remove a card's function). Tiers are pure quantity: 1/2/3/4/6 uses, 1/1/1/2/3 casts a turn. GRADE: never a key, never a solvent - 0% alone on every finale of every run tested at every tier - and NOT half of any gate. A glass is worth exactly one Rookie move plus the durations that move would have burned, which is inside the noise floor of a 32-trial cell. It pays only beside a partner whose payoff lands on an ENEMY phase (Candle L9: poison-dart 13% alone -> 72-81% paired; Candle decoy 47/44/69/31 -> 56/56/91/69) and is neutral-to-negative beside snare, scarecrow and freeze-ray. KEPT as the catalogue's best TRAP filler (the seat it holds in The Hayloft revenge-27 and The Quarry revenge-32). Two runs were built to gate on it and neither did (revenge-29 The Candle, revenge-31 The Hearth, both at stage idea). Full reasoning: docs/revenge-abilities.md, docs/ability-pairs.md, .claude/run-level-design.md.

items.name: Scarecrow
items.notes: Stand a straw Rookie on an empty square (free action). For 1/2/2/2/3 enemy turns the court and the king plan against a view where the straw IS Rookie (rook-form; a queen from T4) and the real Rookie is a blocker nothing can capture or hunt: hunters charge the straw, guards fear its lines, and the king flees from IT, which steers him because his flee is deterministic (farthest safe square from the threat). Striking the straw destroys it and wastes the army's action, no credit, no stun; at T5 the striker dies instead. The straw blocks Rookie's own moves and her summons like a body. One straw at a time. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: The Hayloft
items.notes: Signature pair SCARECROW + KNIGHT-HOP (he runs the wrong way, onto your line). Signature = a gabled stone roof over ranks 4-6 with an 18-square loft above it; kit scarecrow/knight-hop/aegis/hourglass. Finale gate MET at T1: L7-L10 none 0%, every single kit card 0%, pair 66/69/63/75% (serial, 32 trials). Four different finale decisions: steer / blindfold / which straw / where the straw can stand. Known tier break: knight-hop:4 (two uses) solos the finale 88-100%, the Parapet's caveat. Full runs 25% random, 65% pair-pool. Scarecrow is at TESTING so this run is playtest-only.

items.name: The Candle
items.notes: Hourglass + poison-dart combo run (let the fuse burn). Signature: a stone gallery over ranks 7-8 with a 2x2 turret and ONE stair, a bishop bricked into a niche as the only remote stun, and a procession of pawns as the visible clock. GATE 3-OF-4 at L7-L10 (T1, Normal, 32 trials): no-ability 0/0/0/3, hourglass alone 0 at EVERY tier, magnet 0 at every tier, aegis 0 at every tier, pair 63/69/78/69. MISS: poison-dart alone reads 78/75/13/78 — structural, not tuning: a glass-turn and an idle move produce the same enemy phases (the glass only saves one MOVE), MOVE_LIMIT_FLOOR=6 forbids the moveLimit 5 a one-move gate needs, and the dart has no line of sight or timing limit so the fuse can always be synced to the walk. Full runs 15% random / 10% pair-only.

items.name: The Squint
items.notes: Signature pair COUP + DUCHESS (his sentry on the throne, him on the doorstep). Signature = a blind cell whose throne is sealed on rank, file AND diagonal, with one diagonal DOORSTEP and one long squint-diagonal that reaches the post and never the throne. Kit coup/duchess/aegis/magnet. Finale gate MET at T1: L7-L10 none 0%, every single kit card 0%, pair 94/91/91/94 (32 trials). abilityTierCaps { coup: 2, duchess: 3 } — coup:3 solos the finale 100% (any guard within 2, plus a second charge, lets him be hopped across the board via wandering hunters); duchess:4 reads 31/31/28/56. Four different finale decisions: the line / which guard / the shuttered lane / the throne given back. HONEST MISS: pair is 91-94%, not 60-80 — the pair's line is 2-3 moves from any start and a perfect-information bot does not misstep a walk; every knob measured (clock does nothing, punishers are a cliff at 3-13%). Full runs 10% random, 70% pair-pool. Coup is at TESTING so this run is playtest-only.

items.name: The Hearth
items.notes: Hourglass + Snare test. COMBO GATE NOT MET: none/hourglass/aegis/magnet all 0% on L6-L10 at every tier, but SNARE ALONE reads 44-75% and adding the glass makes the snare line WORSE on nearly every level (L6 75->66, L9 72->53, L10 44->38, 32 trials). Hourglass cannot extend a snare hold (a glass-turn burns one of the two moves the hold grants), snare is a free action so the flee is already paid for by her threatening move, and at T3+ hourglassHoldsKing stops the king fleeing during a glass-turn at all - the pair is an antiPair. Ships as an honest SINGLE-KEY run on a new signature (a free-standing stone fireplace whose mouth faces away from Rookie); 4/40 full clears random picks, 4/40 pair-pool. Stays at idea - not marked built.

items.name: The Quarry
items.notes: Signature pair SHOVE + MAGNET (pull the plug, roll the wall). Signature: a one-thick vertical FACE on file f with a single CUT, a two-file LEDGE behind it, and exactly one non-fixed stone per level. Gate MET at 32 trials, Normal: L7-L10 no-ability 0%, every kit single (shove/magnet/aegis/hourglass) 0% at EVERY tier T1-T5, pair 72/59/72/66. No abilityTierCaps needed - fixed stones gate Shove better than a cap. Full runs 20% random picks, 10% pair-pool. Shove is TESTING, so playtest-only.

items.name: The Warren
items.notes: Snare + Boulder. HONEST MISS: singles gate holds (every kit card 0% on L7-L10) but the pair reads only 19-34%, far below the 60-80 band — the run is too hard, not too easy, and the clock is not the limiter (L7 read 13% at 10 moves, 38% at more). Committed with its numbers; NOT on the playtest page. Needs the winning line shortened before it can ship.

items.name: The Dogleg
items.notes: Combo run for the signature pair TWIN + REWIND ('insurance on a one-charge body'; the pair the discovery harness proved could gate, data/run-playtest/combo-library/rewind+twin). VERB: spend a body where nothing survives, then take the killing back — the only run in the catalogue whose answer is an UNDO. SIGNATURE: an L-shaped stone wall seals the king's corridor with no gap at all — every orthogonal boundary square is wall — so no rook, bishop or queen ray, no pawn and no walk ever enters it. The one way in is the NOOK: a corridor square whose only free neighbour outside is DIAGONAL, the outside corner of the dogleg. A line cannot turn that corner; a body BORN there is already inside. Inside, the single square that attacks the king (the POST) is covered by a jammed knight, so any rook standing on it dies — which is why the answer is a body you can get back. FOUR FINALE LINES, four different jobs for the body: L7 die on the post (one slide, seven moves); L8 buy the post (it is occupied by a knotted bishop, so the body's one move must be a CAPTURE); L9 wait first (the king is a rank lower, so the top of the shaft is a waiting room and the body must turn the corner and survive a phase before taking the post); L10 both, on the longest walk, mirrored, four body-moves against a four-turn leash. SERIAL NUMBERS (32 trials, jobs=1, Normal): none 0/0/0/0, twin 0/0/0/0, rewind 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, poison-dart 0/0/0/0, twin+rewind 69/78/63/63 — gate MET, inside the 60-80% band. Every other kit pair 0-9%. FULL RUNS (40 each): random offer picks 0/40, pool pinned to the pair 5/40 = 13%. TIER CAVEAT: abilityTierCaps twin:2. Twin T3 is the second charge and it breaks L7/L8 (75%/66% alone) because the first body can trade itself for the executioner; L9 and L10 are gated at every twin tier because their executioners sit in pockets no body can reach.

items.name: The Picket
items.notes: Signature pair PAGE + AEGIS, verb: take a capture you do not survive, then grow a body on the one square he cannot leave. Neither card had a home (Aegis was a trap filler in eight kits and never half a pair; Page had never been in any shipped kit). Constant signature: a solid back wall (a8-e8 + e7/f7 stone, which is what stops a Page promoting into a controlled queen and what bricks the SECOND door f7), a two-square king pen on a DIAGONAL (g8/h7, the one shape a lone rook can never hold and one pawn ends), a jammed bishop GUARD on g7 defended by a frozen warden pawn on f8, and a jammed bishop GATE standing on h6 - the only square in the game from which a Page can be planted on the door. The line: shield, take the defended gate, plant the pawn on h7, it takes the king. Four finale levels vary the ROAD not the finish (L7 one hunter; L8 mirror, two hunters, refuse the free shield; L9 near-side hunters so the waiting squares are watched; L10 mirror, two hunters, two enemies a turn) - the plant is instantaneous so there is no second beat inside the finish to vary, and that gap is written into the header rather than dressed up. Serial numbers of record (jobs=1, 32 trials, normal, T1 cards) L7-L10: none 0/0/0/0, page 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, rewind 0/0/0/0, page+aegis 66/75/66/66. Full runs: 12.5% random clears (5/40), 15% with pool=page,aegis (6/40). TIER CAVEAT and cap: abilityTierCaps { aegis: 1 } - aegis:2 breaks all four finales at 100% (a second charge pays the gate AND tanks the warden when she takes the guard on g7, and a rook on g7 covers the whole step); page:3 and page:5 stay at 0% because the walls, not a cap, answer promotion. tier-cap-audit passes with aegis still offered 1364x as a new pick.

items.name: The Turnstile
items.notes: Concept type (A): the unbuilt harness-proven pair QUEEN PULSE + SMOKE, verb 'make him stop running, then arrive on a line no rook can walk'. Kit = queen-pulse / smoke / aegis / magnet, all four LIVE. SIGNATURE — THE TURNSTILE: on every level his 2x2 court is walled into the NE corner with exactly one door (g6) and one stone POST set directly outside it (g5), so no rank and no file passes through the doorway and only a 45-degree move can enter; L1/L2/L6 remove the post to prove that getting in was never the problem. FOUR FINALE LINES, all different: L7 two roads (h5 stops at the door and the cover is spent two moves later on g8; f5 runs the diagonal straight to h7 and both cards go down together); L8 the door IS the line (king on g8, so smoke must ride the crossing turn or the level is lost); L9 the post MOVES to the west wall (door f7, post e7, approach along the flank); L10 the kill square is INSIDE the pen (king on h7, only g7 and h8 hold him, two enemies a turn). SERIAL NUMBERS OF RECORD (32 trials, jobs=1, normal): no-ability 0/0/0/0, queen-pulse alone 0/0/0/0, smoke alone 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, the pair 72/63/72/72 — inside the 60-80 band. Mid ladder: L1-L2 free with no ability, L3-L6 all 0% bare with queen-pulse 100 on L3-L6, aegis 100 on L4-L5 and smoke 100 on L6. FULL RUNS (40): 10% random picks, 40% with pool=queen-pulse,smoke. TIER CAVEAT: queen-pulse breaks the gate at T2 (100/0/100/59) because a second queen move covers a whole 2x2 from inside it, so abilityTierCaps pins it at T1; smoke, aegis and magnet all read 0% at their ceilings; tier-cap-audit passes with 0 violations. Known soft spot, reported not chased: the 10% random-pick rate is an offer-preference artefact — L3 is gated on queen-pulse specifically and the bot took it 11 times in 40 runs against 43/32/31 for the other three cards.
